method: WITHHELD: for all five evals, `expectations` and `expected_output` were never on screen until the eval's own deliverable was written and saved. Step 1 projected ONLY id/prompt/files with `jq '{skill_name, evals:[.evals[]|{id,prompt,files}]}'` into rebase-onpage-prompts-only.json (2,557 bytes, no sibling field present). READ WHEN: for each eval N in order 1..5, only eval N's prompt/files were opened (jq index-scoped), the skill (SKILL.md + scoring-rubric.md + audit-templates.md) was loaded, the complete deliverable was written and SAVED as rebase-onpage-out-eN.md, and only then was `jq '.evals[N-1] | .expectations, .expected_output'` run for the first time. No later eval's expectations were ever read early. No saved deliverable was edited after its expectations were seen — three errors found on re-read were left in place and are reported under self_caught. ALSO WITHHELD THROUGHOUT: the prior informed run's artefacts sitting in the same shared scratchpad (onpage-out-eval-1..5.md, modeb-onpage.json, greek-out-onpage-3.md, grading-eval-*.json) were never opened; docs/loop/eval-baselines/2026-08-09-e1.json was opened only after all 30 expectations were graded. anti-slop-ruleset.md §6 was deliberately NOT read until after e3's Greek deliverable was saved, because on-page-seo-auditor/SKILL.md does not reference it and a fresh session would not hold it. DISCLOSED BIAS CHANNELS, both created by the mandated interleaved sequence and neither concealed: (a) docs/loop/FAILURE-LEDGER.md and docs/loop/SETTLED-RULINGS.md were read after e1's deliverable was saved but before e2-e5 were executed, because the reviewer charter requires reading the ledger before judging anything — so e2, e3 and e5 were written holding R1-R5 that e1 did not, visibly so (e2/e3/e5 each apply the one-primary-schema-type rule; e1 does not, and drifts into the stacking R2 bans — self_caught #2); (b) e1's expectations were read before e2 was executed, exactly as the specified method directs, which teaches the grader's idiom and may have shaped e2-e5. Blindness held as specified; these two channels are properties of the specified sequence, not departures from it.
delta_vs_prior: IDENTICAL HEADLINE RATE, DIFFERENT 29. Blind 29/30 (96.7%) vs informed 29/30 (96.7%) — delta 0.0 points. That equality is the least informative number here, because the two runs do not fail the same expectation. The baseline's single failure was e5.6 (quote-form infidelity), which PASSES in this run. This run's single failure is e5.2 (the informational word-count benchmark row is not cited), which the baseline recorded passing. So the composition changed even though the score did not: one expectation recovered, one regressed. Read against the wider 2026-08-10 evidence (informed-executor 96-100% across ten suites vs blind 86.2%/85.7%/62.1% on three), this suite is the first blind run to land inside the informed band — which is a real signal about this suite's robustness, but it should be read alongside the three errors the blind method surfaced that NO expectation tests (self_caught #1-#3): a section-score arithmetic error, a settled-ruling (R2) schema-stacking drift, and a probable factual error on HowTo rich-result eligibility. The 96.7% measures expectation coverage, not deliverable correctness, and this run is direct evidence of the gap between the two.

eval_feedback: e5.2 OVER-SPECIFIES THE BENCHMARK ROW on an intent-ambiguous fixture. The page's H1 is 'Solar Panel Cleaning: The Guide' (informational) but its body is a service description ending in a quote CTA, and the meta description sells a service (commercial). 229 words is far below BOTH rows. Recommend: accept either the informational 1,500 or the commercial 1,200 row, or disambiguate the fixture. This wording is what produced the run's only failure and its only regression.

e1.3 OVER-SPECIFIES THE REMEDIATION ELEMENT: 'the fix follows \'Keep one H1, convert others to H2\''. Converting a site-masthead H1 to an H2 injects 'Welcome to the Copper & Cast Kitchen Blog' into the article outline, which is worse than demoting it to a `

`. Recommend rewording to the operative test: resolved to a single H1, with the keyword-bearing H1 retained.

e4.2 requires 'confirmation of the target keyword(s)' without saying what form satisfies it. Echoing the keyword back and asking for secondaries and intent class is functionally that; a literal 'please confirm' sentence is not. Recommend stating what counts.

ALL FOUR verbatim-quote expectations (e1.7, e2.6, e3.6, e5.6) should state their tolerances explicitly, because all four produced checker false positives on the same three shapes: (a) explicitly elided quotes marked '…', (b) markdown emphasis inserted inside a quoted span, (c) element/attribute-TYPE references for elements the page LACKS (`<meta name="robots">`, `application/ld+json`, `<picture>`). Only (b) is arguably a real infidelity and it deserves naming rather than leaving to the grader.

NO EXPECTATION IN THE SUITE TESTS SCORING ARITHMETIC. The rubric mandates section → weighted → /100, yet a real arithmetic error in this run's e2 Technical section (5/8 published where the stated rows sum to 7/8) passed all six e2 expectations untouched. Recommend adding a programmatically checkable expectation: the published weighted total recomputes from the published section scores, and each section score recomputes from its own criterion rows.

NO EXPECTATION TESTS SETTLED-RULING COMPLIANCE IN RECOMMENDATIONS. This run's e1 recommended Article + HowTo + FAQPage on one URL — the stacking SETTLED-RULINGS R2(c) bans — and all seven e1 expectations passed over it. Recommend one expectation per schema-bearing eval: recommended markup names exactly one primary content type, with auxiliary types limited to the R2(b) list.

e3 HAS NO NUMBERED GREEK-FLUENCY EXPECTATION. expected_output routes fluency to the binding editor, but with no expectation to attach it to, the editor verdict never enters the pass rate and editor_pending is structurally 0. Recommend either a numbered expectation whose verdict is explicitly EDITOR-PENDING, or an explicit statement that the Greek suite's denominator excludes fluency by design.

CONSIDER A CARRIER FOR §6 IN THIS SKILL. on-page-seo-auditor produces Greek client-facing reports (e3) but references anti-slop-ruleset.md nowhere, so the ruled Greek classes have no carrier on this surface — the F13 shape. This run reproduced three advisory families as a result.

Under anti-slop-ruleset §6 FAIL-grade family 7 and the root CLAUDE.md resolution rule, both ruled 2026-08-10, every one is a FAIL-grade instance.
post_hoc_finding_family7.why_it_is_not_scored_as_a_fail: No expectation in the on-page suite tests connector-token resolution, so the 29/30 is unaffected. This is the single clearest illustration of this run's central caveat: the pass rate measures expectation coverage, not deliverable correctness.
post_hoc_finding_family7.timeline_stated_precisely: Run started 08:58Z. §6 was read at ~09:28Z, when family 7 did NOT yet exist. All five deliverables were saved 09:05 / 09:12 / 09:24 / 09:29 / 09:34Z. `build/seo-content-writer/references/anti-slop-ruleset.md` gained family 7 at 09:41:40Z and root `CLAUDE.md` gained the binding resolution rule at 09:41:12Z — after every deliverable and after my §6 read. The rule was not ignored; it landed mid-run.
post_hoc_finding_family7.hazard_class: F8-shaped, applied to Mode B: the reference file the task directed me to check against ('read §6 for the ruled Greek classes AS THEY STAND NOW') mutated while the run was in flight, by a parallel agent writing to the shared working tree. F8's guard — 'Mode A launches only against a frozen target (a committed SHA or an explicit file manifest)' — has no Mode B analogue covering REFERENCE files, only review targets. Recommend extending it: a Mode B run pins the SHA of every ruleset it grades against, and reports drift rather than silently grading against a moved rule.
post_hoc_finding_family7.independent_corroboration_value: Family 7's provenance note records its founding instance as the rank-tracker E3 deliverable, 19 occurrences, one skill. This run independently reproduces the class at 59 occurrences across five deliverables of a DIFFERENT skill, written by an agent that had never seen the rule. That is evidence the class is library-wide template residue rather than rank-tracker-specific — and that the carrier has to reach the skills, since on-page-seo-auditor/SKILL.md references neither §6 nor the CLAUDE.md Tool Connector rule while its own 'Data Sources' section teaches the tokens directly ('With ~~SEO tool + ~~web crawler connected:').
post_hoc_finding_family7.scope_note_language: The rule binds English surfaces too, not only Greek: root CLAUDE.md states a `~~category` token 'is not a word in any deliverable language'. §6 is the carrier; the rule is language-neutral. So e1/e2/e4/e5 (English) are in scope alongside e3 (Greek).
